$comment: Release-only upgrade rehearsal (docs/operations/upgrades.md#release-gate-upgrade-rehearsal). sources lists exactly the releases an installation can upgrade from: the candidate baseline's upgradeFromRelease (which adopts the baseline first) and any later release whose tree already records the candidate's baseline identity. plan.mjs refuses any other source. For every source, the candidate upgrades one install per dataset. Datasets are generated by the SOURCE release's own tooling, because a real install holds data its own version wrote. Every class in requiredDatasetClasses must name at least one dataset, and plan.mjs refuses otherwise. Never wire this into push or pull_request CI.

defaultGate.$comment: Release default: oldest plus latest source (sources-list order, oldest first) on the representative populated dataset. The full matrix stays available opt-in (workflow_dispatch full_matrix). Never wire either into push or pull_request CI.

datasets.description: A bootstrapped install with no activity: the default org only.
One general contractor, one quarter of seeded activity.

USD parent with EUR and CAD subsidiaries plus an elimination subsidiary: FX rates, foreign-currency trade with realized FX, month-end revaluation, intercompany journals, a consolidation run, and closed periods. Seeded by the source release's own posting kernel (no raw ledger inserts).

~1,020,000 journal_lines over 36 months plus payroll runs and stubs, stock counts with a few hundred thousand lines, and small volumes across tables that migrations commonly rewrite or validate. Seeded by the source release's own posting kernel through the bulk path (draft entries, posted header-only documents, one flip to posted, applications last, one timeout-free maintenance transaction per month).
Every sample-company template the source release can prepare.
Recurring-revenue and services companies over a fiscal year-end.
Endurance loop across a year-end and a leap day, with the adversarial probes: backdating into closed periods, posted edits, over-application, reversal symmetry, void and recreate.
